results.description: Programming-Language-Benchmarks kernels via the dotnet tool
notes: build stage ok (dotnet --task build took 22920 ms)

langs=elixir (the tool's elixir environment only, driven with --no-docker); measured 8 kernel run(s): coro-prime-sieve/1000=352 ms, coro-prime-sieve/4000=2554 ms, edigits/100000=686 ms, edigits/250001=2951 ms, helloworld/QwQ=187 ms, pidigits/4000=418 ms, pidigits/8000=1205 ms, spectral-norm/2000=3422 ms
excluded 2 kernel run(s) the tool reported with timeMS=0 — its marker for a run it could not time (aborted at the problem's declared timeout): spectral-norm/4000, spectral-norm/8000

budgets.reason: no `baseline` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: A gross-regression alarm for the Rust boot median (the m17 rounds read 289-546 ms under a 1-min load of 3-92; quieter sessions read ~280-400 ms), not an SLO — a shared host can double it without a code change, so the load-robust judgement is the rust/sys ratio row.

budgets.reason: no `baseline` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: Catches a hang or an order-of-magnitude tail regression (the matched m17 rounds read 291-485 ms p99, with a single 1702 ms outlier on a heavily loaded A/B round), not an SLO: a boot's p99 is a handful of samples, so this row only notices a gross failure.

budgets.reason: no `baseline` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: The load-robust startup judgement: recorded matched-round ratios are 2.2-3.05x (m16 reached 3.79x), so 6x is a regression alarm with headroom above every recorded round — not a target, and deliberately not so tight that ordinary host drift trips it.

budgets.reason: no `baseline` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: The same instrument for the tail; recorded p99 ratios track the p50 ones (2.1-3.4x) because a boot's p99 is a handful of samples, so the same 6x alarm applies — not an SLO for a shared host.

budgets.reason: no `baseline` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: The oracle's own tail, recorded at 105-153 ms across m17: a host artifact big enough to move the far less load-sensitive `sys` side shows up here too, so it cannot be misread as a Rust regression — and 400 ms is deliberately loose because this row exists to attribute, not to gate.

budgets.reason: no `cowboy` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: The request-tail budget on the I/O-bound target, recorded at 3.03-3.59 ms p99 while serving ~198k req/s through a real Cowboy release: 5 ms leaves room for a loaded host yet still flags a real latency regression; it reads the summary the cowboy row actually records (`latency_ms` — there is no separate p99 metric) and it is sys-only because the Rust runtime cannot boot an OTP release.

budgets.reason: no `list_walk` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: The per-element dispatch budget for the standing per-unit gap, recorded at 22.6-48.2 ns/element across m17 (the oracle reads 2.3-2.8): roughly forty times today's figure, so it is a regression alarm for the engine's dispatch path and not a parity target — the gap itself is `beam_engine`'s to close.

budgets.reason: no `copy_bound` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: The messaging budget for the two-process send/receive round trip, recorded at 8091-12450 ns/op across m17 (the oracle reads 1497-1943): ~1.6x above the worst recorded round, so it is a regression alarm rather than a parity target, and it is not a hard ceiling on a contended host.

budgets.reason: no `gc_bound` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: The GC-churn budget for allocate-and-abandon, recorded at 66.4k-106k ns/op across m17 (the oracle reads 4.3k-5.0k): ~1.9x above the worst recorded round, a regression alarm for a figure whose collection count the row does not claim — not a parity target.

budgets.reason: no `file_io` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: A first-pass regression alarm for the file-I/O workload class's write-then-read round trip: no measured figure backs it yet (the workload is reported not-measured until it exists and runs), so it is a placeholder alarm, not a calibrated budget.

budgets.reason: no `gc_class` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: A first-pass regression alarm for the GC-class workload's two-process round trip: like `file_io` it is a placeholder until the workload exists and runs, and it stays not-measured (never a pass, never a failure) until then, so the limit is not yet evidence-backed.
